open_points.unit: 30_modules.md:Facts several modules touch, and their one owner
open_points.subject: persistence of run-derived StoredValues
open_points.text: StoredValue M21 and value bytes are written "always through `store.put_value_bytes`", but `run_values.deliver_input` "writes what the source still needs written through `store.record_change`", and `run_values` owns "writing each through `store.record_change`".
open_points.question: Which store capability writes the StoredValue record and its bytes for a value derived by `run_values`, and are those writes one store call or separate calls?
options: `put_value_bytes` publishes the bytes and `record_change` inserts the StoredValue record
`put_value_bytes` writes both the bytes and the StoredValue record
`record_change` performs both operations internally, including the `put_value_bytes` work
open_points.default_guess: Use `put_value_bytes` for the bytes and `record_change` for the StoredValue record.

open_points.unit: 30_modules.md:Facts several modules touch, and their one owner
open_points.subject: unwritten mapped values
open_points.text: `run_graph` has `run_values.assemble_mapped_lists` "build and measure without writing", while the same section says "No module below `runs` reads a value that is not written".
open_points.question: May `run_values` and `run_graph` construct, inspect and pass an in-memory mapped list before its StoredValue is written, or must the no-unwritten-value rule apply to them too?
options: Allow an explicit transient in-memory exception for assembly and measurement
Write the derived list before `run_graph` or `run_values` may inspect it
Keep the rule only for values delivered to `sandbox` or `effects`, not internal derivation
open_points.default_guess: Treat transient assembly and measurement as an explicit exception; require persistence before delivery to an executing node.

open_points.unit: 30_modules.md:Facts several modules touch, and their one owner
open_points.subject: recovery after an unknown attempt was resolved not_applied
open_points.text: "`ElementWaiting` with another reason rewrites only the waiting point — the element is not reached" and "`ElementNotReached` — no NodeExecution and no requested approval ... makes the run `running` again", but later "a wait for an approval never requested — an attempt the owner resolved `not_applied` — is reached again for its fresh approval".
open_points.question: What conclusion does `effects.operation_element_conclusion` return after an `outcome_unknown` NodeExecution's attempt has been resolved `not_applied` but no fresh approval has yet been requested, so recovery knows to reach the element?
options: Return `ElementNotReached` despite the existing earlier NodeExecution
Return `ElementWaiting(owner_approval)` with an additional fact that no requested approval exists
Have `runs` inspect approval and attempt records separately
open_points.default_guess: Return a distinct needs-reach conclusion that causes `runs` to mark the run running and reach the element.

open_points.subject: mapped-node aggregate conclusion under A13 rule 6
open_points.text: `run_graph` owns only "A13 rules 2, 4, 5, 7 and 8", while `run_values` must not own "what ... a list over the ceiling concludes" and `runs` must not own "readiness, guards, propagation or the run's derived status"; no section explicitly assigns the remaining rule 6 decisions that a mapped node succeeds only when all elements succeed, fails when an element fails, or fails when a delivered list exceeds the ceiling.
open_points.question: Which module owns the non-value conclusions of A13 rule 6, including aggregate mapped-node success or failure and the no-record failure caused by an oversized delivered list?
options: `run_graph` derives all mapped-node aggregate conclusions and `runs` only records or acts on its plan
`runs` owns mapped-node aggregate conclusions as part of executing the map
Split them explicitly: `run_graph` owns conclusions from element records and `runs` owns the oversized-list conclusion
open_points.default_guess: Assign all mapped-node aggregate conclusions to `run_graph`, with `run_values` supplying measurements and `runs` applying the plan.
